subject: Sanctum: CI token rotation and change-ownership appendix

From: LumenBank Security <sec-assessor@lumenbank.com>

Cc: Avery Systems Legal <legal@averysystems.com>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2029 09:10:00 -0500
Subject: Request: CI token rotation history + change-ownership trail for 'Sanctum' deployment

Hi Camila,

We're wrapping up the SIG assessment for LumenBank's integration with your hosted model endpoint (codename 'Sanctum'). The assessor needs:
- A concise token rotation history for the CI runners that deploy Sanctum (last 12 months) with dates and actor IDs.
- Change-ownership matrix describing who authorized deploys and handovers when the runner config or keystore changed.
- A short note on emergency hotfix procedure and who can approve temporary deploy creds.

Please attach the artifacts where possible (redacted IDs are fine) and indicate any outstanding gaps. We'd like these by EOD Wednesday to keep our audit schedule.

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Senior Security Assessor, LumenBank
sec-assessor@lumenbank.com

--

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request: CI token rotation history + change-ownership trail for 'Sanctum' deployment

Hi Daniel — thanks for the specifics. We're compiling a scoped appendix for the Sanctum deployment and can provide:

1) Token rotation timeline (redacted runner IDs): attached PDF 'sanctum-ci-token-rotation-log.pdf' — includes rotation events, issued_by, replaced_by, and rotation_reason for the past 12 months.
2) Change-ownership matrix: CSV 'change-ownership-matrix.csv' that maps deployable components to on-call/owner and authorization method (canary tag, prod-approve ticket id).
3) Emergency hotfix procedure: short snippet in 'ci-runner-policy-snippet.txt' with temporary-cred issuance flow, TTL, and required approvers.

Quick notes/limitations: the token rotation log pulls from our ephemeral secrets service; the logs include operator usernames (internal) and the ticket ref when present. For a small subset of rotations executed by automation (rotations triggered by policy), the human actor is listed as 'automation/secret-rotator' — we can provide additional telemetry if you need process logs.

I'll attach the items here and loop Mina for any further evidence you may require (e.g., PR references for the change that triggered the rotation).

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Partner Success, Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.com

Attachments:
- sanctum-ci-token-rotation-log.pdf (redaction: runner UUIDs partially masked)
- change-ownership-matrix.csv

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Daniel Park <sec-assessor@lumenbank.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2029 08:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: CI token rotation history + change-ownership trail for 'Sanctum' deployment

Thanks Camila — adding a few clarifications from the security engineering side.

- The rotation log includes both manual rotations (requested via ticket) and automated rotations (policy-driven). We marked each entry with 'trigger:manual' or 'trigger:policy'.
- For manual rotations, we include the originating PR if the rotation followed a code change; where available we've included the PR link. Where the PR touches secrets/config, we've redacted blob contents but kept commit hashes.
- Change-ownership matrix: owners are scoped by component (deploy runner, keystore, release pipeline). The CSV column 'temporary_approver' lists on-call escalation contacts; these are phone/email tags rather than personal phone numbers.
- Emergency hotfix approval path: two approvers required if the change bypasses the normal CI gating (one infrastructure owner + one engineering manager). We included the fallback 'oncall-sre' umbrella identity in the policy snippet.

If LumenBank would like, we can export a compact PR-to-rotation mapping (PR id -> rotation event) for a 90-day sample. That is typically helpful for assessors who want to trace a code change through to a secrets change.

Mina Haddad
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request: CI token rotation history + change-ownership trail for 'Sanctum' deployment

Hi Daniel — quick follow-up after Mina's note.

- Retention: rotation audit entries are retained for 400 days in our compliance ledger (we keep a rolling 365-day primary window plus a 35-day buffer used for cross-region replication delays).
- Sample export: attached a 90-day PR-to-rotation CSV (redacted) as part of the Drive link: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/SDLC/Sanctum/rotation-log. The CSV has columns: pr_id, pr_url, rotation_time, rotation_actor, ticket_ref.
- Legal/contract note: Avery, we've flagged the sample exports as redacted; please advise if LumenBank needs unredacted identifiers under NDA — we can route through the enterprise request flow.

Let us know if you need a short recorded walkthrough (10-15m) of how rotations are initiated from CI and how the keystore actor mapping works — we can schedule with SRE.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Director, Reliability Engineering, Redwood Inference
